blocks.html: A child in Latin is called INFANS until the age of seven years a, as it were unable to speak (quasi nescius fari), that is to say, as not knowing how to speak: because, being in this tender age, he can scarcely yet untie his tongue to pronounce the words distinctly. Whence Chrysippus said that children who are already beginning to babble and to pronounce some words may be said almost to speak, but in truth they say nothing, nor speak at all. Thus one must not be astonished if, in the matter of which we treat, the prisoner, who had been brought very small, and at the age of little more than two years, from the Basque country, had not retained the language, which he never understood nor ever knew how to speak.
